clue.text: In a moderate year, male becomes extremely powerful

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the male abbreviation is placed in among the other pieces, which surround it

parts.note: light, as in a light breeze or light exercise, means moderate

explanation.surface: Someone of middling ability, in an average year, becomes enormously powerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' tells you to put M inside the run A + LIGHT + Y, giving A-L-M-IGHT-Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Almighty describes a being with unlimited strength, the greatest possible might.

clue.text: Football team second entering stadium, left last

indicators.note: the second abbreviation goes into the stadium word, so it is entering it

parts.note: an arena is a stadium or sports ground

explanation.surface: A football club's second string comes into the ground, with someone who departed bringing up the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entering' puts S inside ARENA to make ARSENA; 'last' tells you L goes at the end. Arsenal is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenal is a well-known professional football club based in north London.

clue.text: Sort of verse dandy composed at first

parts.note: a macaroni was an eighteenth-century fop or dandy

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word composed is taken

explanation.surface: A kind of poetry that a fashionable gent wrote first of all.
explanation.walkthrough: A MACARONI was a showy dandy in Georgian Britain; add C, the opening letter of 'composed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaronic verse mixes words from two languages, often Latin with a vernacular, for comic effect.

clue.text: Fabric in middle of swinging hammock

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words swinging hammock, spanning the join

explanation.surface: Cloth in the centre of a hammock that sways.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across swinGING HAMmock.
explanation.definitionFit: Gingham is a cotton cloth woven in checks or stripes.

clue.text: Give new order to earn the capital

indicators.note: rearranging the letters of earn and the gives them a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder as written
anagram fodder as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to rearrange things so as to make the money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give new order to' rearranges EARN THE; 'capital' looks financial beside 'earn' but means a capital city. Teheran is an older spelling of Tehran, Iran's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Teheran, now usually Tehran, is the capital city of Iran.

clue.text: Programme in two short parts — that's funny

definitions.text: Programme in two short parts — that's funny

parts.words: Programme in two short parts — that's funny
parts.note: the name of this kind of television show is built from two clipped words, one of them meaning comedy

explanation.surface: A broadcast in two brief instalments, which happens to be comic.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a clipped form of 'situation comedy': two shortened parts, SIT and COM, the second meaning something funny.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitcom is a comedy series built around recurring characters in a fixed setting.

clue.text: Not the main topic in party publication

parts.note: a side is a party or faction in a dispute
an issue is one published edition of a magazine or paper

explanation.surface: Something that isn't central to a political party's newsletter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' suggests politics but simply means SIDE, as in a side in an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A side issue is a secondary question, away from the principal matter under discussion.

clue.text: Hard person to hug passionately, that's quickly seen

indicators.note: a passionate hug is wild, so the letters of to hug are thrown about

parts.note: anagram fodder as written
that is, written in quick shorthand, is the abbreviation i.e.

explanation.surface: A tough character to embrace with ardour, as is soon apparent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passionately' rearranges TO HUG into TOUGH; 'that's quickly seen' is the short form i.e. (id est, that is).
explanation.definitionFit: A toughie is informal for a hard, tough person or a difficult problem.

clue.text: Part of chapter in Old Testament turned upside-down

indicators.note: the part of a chapter is placed in the abbreviation for the scriptures

parts.note: a verse is a numbered division within a chapter of the Bible

explanation.surface: A section of a biblical chapter that was turned on its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned upside-down' looks like a reversal signal but is the definition: overset is an old word for capsized.
explanation.definitionFit: Overset is an old word meaning overturned or capsized.

clue.text: Fastest-moving pointer a hunter could have?

definitions.meaning: on a clock the quickest pointer is the one sweeping round each minute
a hunter is a pocket watch with a hinged cover, which carries such a pointer; also, a hunting horse may be bought used

explanation.surface: Wondering what the quickest dial pointer of a huntsman's watch might be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointer' tempts towards dogs and hunting, but it is the hand of a watch; a hunter is a pocket watch with a lid.
explanation.definitionFit: The seconds pointer moves fastest on a dial; a hunter watch has one, and anything not new is also called that.

clue.text: Church official not hard-hearted as employer

indicators.note: the hard abbreviation is not kept, so it comes out of the church official

parts.note: an usher shows people to their seats in a church
H, abbreviation for hard (as on pencils), is the heart of the church official word

explanation.surface: A churchwarden who isn't cruel is the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard-hearted' reads as cruel, but says take H (hard) from the heart of USHER.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is someone who employs or makes use of something.

clue.text: Heavenly spectacle in Yorkshire- Lancashire matches, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a shimmering display of coloured light in the polar sky
matches are things to light fires, and those from northern English counties might jokingly be called so

explanation.surface: A glorious sight in the sky during the Roses cricket matches between two northern counties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Matches' looks like sporting fixtures between Yorkshire and Lancashire, two counties in the north of England, but means lights for striking.
explanation.definitionFit: The aurora borealis is a glowing display seen in high northern skies; lights here also means matches.

clue.text: Programme presenter no longer needed for light duties

definitions.meaning: a broadcaster who introduces and connects items in a show

definitions.text: no longer needed for light duties
definitions.meaning: historically a man who carried a torch to light the way through dark streets, now obsolete

explanation.surface: A TV host who isn't required any more for easy work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light duties' suggests easy work, but refers to carrying a torch: the old link was a burning torch.
explanation.definitionFit: A link man ties a broadcast together; formerly the term named a torch-bearer guiding pedestrians at night.

clue.text: Considered employing a story editor

parts.note: an account is a story or narrative of events

explanation.surface: Thought about hiring a writer of fiction as an editor.
explanation.definitionFit: To account something good is to consider or regard it as such.

clue.text: Views a bit of text, wearing glasses

indicators.note: the glasses put on, or wear, the small piece of text, which sits inside them

parts.note: specs is informal for spectacles, glasses

indicators.note: just the opening letter of text is taken

explanation.surface: Someone reads part of a document with their spectacles on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wearing' puts T, the opening letter of 'text', inside SPECS; A from 'a' comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspects are views or outlooks, ways something appears from a given angle.

clue.text: Porter's dismissal Eric's badly taken to heart

definitions.note: read as porter is, so the definition is the noun porter

indicators.note: the rearranged name is placed at the centre of the dismissal word

parts.note: a congé is a formal dismissal or leave to depart

indicators.note: the letters of the name are arranged badly, scrambled

parts.note: the name as written, the possessive adding no letter

explanation.surface: A doorman is upset that Eric was sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' scrambles the name to CIER; 'taken to heart' sets it in the middle. A congé is a French-derived word for dismissal; 'Porter' is a doorkeeper, not a carrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A concierge is a doorkeeper or hall porter in a hotel or block of flats.

clue.text: Being attacked on board? It's under control

definitions.meaning: in chess, a king under threat from an enemy piece is in this state

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a chess player whose king is threatened is still in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' means a chessboard: a king under attack is in check.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess a threatened king is in that state; held back or restrained also uses the phrase.

clue.text: Gas consumed is a recent issue

parts.note: neon is a noble gas
ate means consumed, eaten

explanation.surface: Fuel use is a topical matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' suggests a topic, but means offspring: a newborn baby.
explanation.definitionFit: A neonate is a newborn child, so very recent offspring.

clue.text: Energetic steps to get weedkiller reduced

parts.note: a hoe is a garden tool used to kill weeds
down means lowered or reduced

explanation.surface: Lively footwork to get herbicide prices cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weedkiller' suggests a chemical but is a garden tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoedown is a lively American folk dance, all vigorous footwork.

clue.text: Specifies what's new in challenges

indicators.note: the new abbreviation goes in the challenges word

parts.note: defies means challenges or dares

explanation.surface: Stating what is novel among a set of contests.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes inside DEFIES, giving DEFI-N-ES.
explanation.definitionFit: To define something is to state it precisely, to set out its meaning or limits.

clue.text: Branch I had set up on border

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the letters are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
a verge is an edge or border, such as a roadside strip

explanation.surface: A branch office I'd established at the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' turns the contraction to DI, which sits on top of the border word in this down clue; 'Branch' is the verb, to fork off.
explanation.definitionFit: To diverge is to branch off in a different direction.

clue.text: Beetle in sack put on carriage

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece put on another sits above it

parts.note: to fire is to sack from a job
a fly was a light horse-drawn carriage for hire

explanation.surface: An insect in a bag is placed on a cart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack' is a bag in the surface, but means dismiss; a FLY is an old one-horse hire carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: The firefly is a nocturnal beetle whose abdomen glows with light.

clue.text: Piece of canvas — or possibly silk, say

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters of silk and say could be rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder as written
anagram fodder as written

explanation.surface: A sheet of canvas, or perhaps silk, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example' but is fodder: SILK SAY rearranges to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A skysail is a small sail set above the royal on a square-rigged ship, a piece of sailcloth.

clue.text: Poet and economist locate this educational establishment

definitions.text: Poet and economist locate this educational establishment

parts.words: Poet and economist locate this educational establishment
parts.note: a college that anyone, whatever their trade, can join and study at from home

explanation.surface: Two scholars track down a particular college.
explanation.walkthrough: A cryptic definition: Britain's distance-learning university admits all comers, poets and economists alike, and needs no finding.
explanation.definitionFit: The Open University is Britain's distance-learning university, open to adults without entry qualifications.

clue.text: Ancient as one silver ring

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Something old, like a single silver band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ancient' seems to mean old, but is an old word for ensign: Othello's Ancient is Shakespeare's villain.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's Othello the villainous ensign is called the Ancient, the old word for standard-bearer.

clue.text: Ground so hard a farmer initially rakes it, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps says these letters may be arranged otherwise

parts.note: anagram fodder as written

indicators.note: just the opening letter of rakes is used

parts.note: anagram fodder as written

explanation.surface: Earth so compacted that a farmer starts raking it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' rearranges A FARMER + R (the start of 'rakes') + IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Terra firma is Latin for firm land, solid earth rather than sea or air.

clue.text: Written in confined circumstances

definitions.meaning: shut up in an enclosure, as livestock are

explanation.surface: Composed while cooped up.
explanation.definitionFit: To pen is to write, and also to shut animals in a fold; both give the past form.

clue.text: Having no complaints, agreed

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of assent, like all right then

explanation.surface: In good health and in agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes someone in fine health, and also serves as a reply of assent.
